summary.title: Programming quotes worth keeping around
summary.one_liner: A personal collection of funny, blunt programming quotes from figures like Dijkstra, Kernighan, Knuth, Torvalds and Larry Wall, mostly about debugging and how developers work.
keywords: bill gates lines of code quote
takeaways: Many well-known programmers have memorable quotes about debugging being harder than writing code.
Writing code as cleverly as possible makes debugging harder, so simplicity is worth preferring (Kernighan).
Measuring progress by lines of code is a poor metric (Gates), and the page recommends remembering Kernighan's warning during hard debugging sessions.
The list also includes jokes about programming languages such as Java vs JavaScript, PHP, Perl and .Net.
summary.summary: This personal blog post gathers about two dozen short programming quotes, each attributed to a named developer or marked anonymous, with no commentary beyond a brief intro. Most quotes are humorous or cynical about debugging, languages, and developer habits. A few longer entries, such as Peter Borum's on the flow state of programming and music, are more reflective. The author closes by naming Kernighan's warning about clever code as the most useful one during hard debugging.
